ui:pages.ramadan.whatIsRamadan.title: What is Ramadan?
keyPoints: Says Ramadan is the ninth month and the fast runs from dawn to sunset: no food, no drink, no sexual intercourse
Says the first revelation of the Quran came during Ramadan (Quran 2:185)
Says the month is also about prayer, reading Quran, giving and how you treat people
ui:pages.ramadan.whatIsRamadan.label: Ramadan guide page > What is Ramadan?

ui:pages.ramadan.forNewMuslims.title: For new Muslims
keyPoints: 'Whatever fasting you manage counts, and you can build up from there': confirm it does not imply Ramadan fasts are optional for a healthy new Muslim

Link label promises what someone who became Muslim during Ramadan owes and does not owe
ui:pages.ramadan.forNewMuslims.label: Ramadan guide page > For new Muslims

ui:pages.ramadan.fastingBasics.title: Fasting basics
keyPoints: Suhoor 'before the Fajr prayer': make sure eating clearly stops at dawn (start of Fajr time), not at the congregational prayer
Attributes 'kissing or touching that leads to ejaculation breaks the fast' to the Hanafi school only (Bukhari 1927); the four schools broadly agree
'If you eat or drink by accident, the fast still stands': the hadith (Bukhari 1933) is about forgetting; schools differ, and Malikis require a make-up day
Exempt list says missed days are made up; elderly people who cannot fast usually pay fidyah instead, and menstruating women may not fast
ui:pages.ramadan.fastingBasics.label: Ramadan guide page > Fasting basics

ui:pages.ramadan.preparing.title: Preparing for Ramadan
keyPoints: 'Learn two short supplications: the intention for fasting, and the dua for breaking it'; the page says intention is in the heart, so confirm what text is meant
Advises shifting sleep earlier and cutting caffeine before Ramadan to avoid withdrawal headaches
Says 'Most people are reasonable about religious observance' when you tell an employer or school
Advises setting money aside for Eid, zakat al-fitr and gifts so the month does not end on a credit card
ui:pages.ramadan.preparing.label: Ramadan guide page > Preparing for Ramadan

ui:pages.ramadan.duringRamadan.title: During Ramadan
keyPoints: Says the dua of someone fasting 'carries particular weight' (hadith-based, e.g. Tirmidhi 3598; its grading is debated)
Says generosity is strongly encouraged in Ramadan (e.g. Bukhari 6) and to pray more, especially Tarawih at the mosque
Health tips: dehydration causes more trouble than hunger, do not skip suhoor, nap, break the fast with dates and water (Sunnah)
preCheckFlags: Hadith-based claims (a fasting person's dua 'carries particular weight'; extra generosity in Ramadan) have no matching source in the Ramadan page's source list
ui:pages.ramadan.duringRamadan.label: Ramadan guide page > During Ramadan

ui:pages.ramadan.tarawihAndCommunity.title: Night prayers and community (tarawih)
keyPoints: Says Tarawih are extra evening prayers after Isha at the mosque in Ramadan and 'leaving partway through is fine'

ui:pages.ramadan.tarawihAndCommunity.label: Ramadan guide page > Night prayers and community (tarawih)

ui:pages.ramadan.laylatAlQadr.title: Laylat al-Qadr (the Night of Power)
keyPoints: Says the Quran calls Laylat al-Qadr better than a thousand months (Quran 97:3)
Says it is sought on the odd nights 21st to 29th; the cited source (Bukhari 2020) is noted only for 'the last ten nights' (odd nights: e.g. Bukhari 2017)
Says the Prophet did i'tikaf every Ramadan until he died (Bukhari 2026) and that i'tikaf is voluntary
Says masjids hosting i'tikaf have their own rules, including for women and shorter stays

ui:pages.ramadan.laylatAlQadr.label: Ramadan guide page > Laylat al-Qadr (the Night of Power)

ui:pages.mentalHealth.faithAndHelp.title: Faith and professional help
keyPoints: Says Islam treats caring for your mind as part of caring for yourself; seeing a counsellor is like seeing a doctor while praying for healing
Says the Prophet and his companions felt grief, sadness and stress (e.g. Bukhari 1303 on his son Ibrahim)
Callout 'tie your camel, then trust in Allah' is called 'a well-known saying'; it is a hadith (Tirmidhi 2517) and its grading should be stated
'Being Muslim does not mean being happy every moment. It means holding onto hope'
preCheckFlags: Paraphrases the 'tie your camel' hadith (Tirmidhi 2517) and says the Prophet felt grief, with no matching source on the page; sunnah-bukhari-1303 exists but is not attached
ui:pages.mentalHealth.faithAndHelp.label: Mental health page > Faith and professional help

ui:pages.mentalHealth.commonExperiences.title: Common experiences
keyPoints: Eating disorders: says the illness exemption from fasting covers an eating disorder; the only source is a UK dietitian article (BDA), not a fiqh source
Alcohol and drugs: talk to your doctor before stopping heavy drinking and call your provincial addiction line; 'a slip is a reason to start again'
Winter mood: CAMH describes SAD as depression recurring in fall or winter, more common far from the equator; light therapy is the main treatment
Evil eye or jinn: says paid healers exploit the fear; confirm framing fits the mainstream belief that the evil eye is real (Bukhari 5740)
Waswas: repeated wudu, restarting prayers or unwanted thoughts about Allah are 'often called waswas, and for some people a form of OCD'; 'OCD is treatable'
Coming back: 'start with the next prayer and a short repentance in your own words'; says nothing about making up prayers missed as a Muslim
Doubts: 'Islam tells you to go looking for knowledge'; 'working through them honestly usually leaves faith stronger'; links 'Am I still Muslim?'
Hate incident: 'keep a record, report it if you choose... Victim services can help'; family conflict: skip debates, set gentle boundaries
preCheckFlags: Winter item says 'Some people sink every November. Isha comes late'; in a Canadian winter Isha is early evening. Late Isha is a summer issue, and linked faq-pry-005 is about summer
ui:pages.mentalHealth.commonExperiences.label: Mental health page > Common experiences

ui:pages.mentalHealth.selfCare.title: Practical self-care
keyPoints: Says dhikr and prayer help when anxiety spikes: repeating 'SubhanAllah' or reciting Al-Fatiha 'can steady a bad moment'
Says repeating 'SubhanAllah' on long breaths 'calms the body and the heart together'
On a worn-out week, 'keep what is required and pause the extras'; points to a plan for hard weeks on the New Muslim basics page
'Enjoying yourself is not un-Islamic'; in winter get morning daylight and plan sleep around the masjid timetable
ui:pages.mentalHealth.selfCare.label: Mental health page > Practical self-care

ui:pages.mentalHealth.seekHelp.title: When to seek professional help
keyPoints: Callout: 'call 9-1-1 or go to the nearest emergency department now', then 'If you are thinking about suicide, call or text 9-8-8 at any hour' (order complies)
Warning signs include 'Thoughts of harming yourself, or wishing you were not alive' and 'Using substances to get through the day'
Says 'Needing help is not weak faith. Islam supports getting treatment' (no hadith cited, e.g. Bukhari 5678)
Tells readers to contact a mental health professional or a crisis line if any listed sign applies
ui:pages.mentalHealth.seekHelp.label: Mental health page > When to seek professional help

ui:pages.mentalHealth.disclaimer.title: Note (disclaimer)
keyPoints: Says the guide is general emotional support and education, not a substitute for therapy or medical advice

ui:pages.mentalHealth.disclaimer.label: Mental health page > Note (disclaimer)

ui:pages.mentalHealth.resources.title: Support resources
keyPoints: Crisis order: 9-1-1 first, then 9-8-8 Suicide Crisis Helpline (call or text, free, 24 hours a day) under 'If you are in danger or thinking about suicide'
Kids Help Phone 1-800-668-6868 or text CONNECT to 686868 (24/7; texts not anonymous); Hope for Wellness 1-855-242-3310 (24/7, First Nations, Inuit, Métis)
ESVA Canada (endingviolencecanada.org) listed for sexual assault centres; its source esva-getting-help is not in the page's source list
Naseeha 1 (866) 627-3342: 24/7 Muslim youth helpline, 'not an emergency service... call 9-1-1 or 9-8-8 first'
Sakeenah 1-888-671-3446 (24/7, domestic violence); Nisa Helpline and Nisa Homes +1 888 711 6472 (8 AM to midnight ET, 14+); Nisa FAQ still shows 1-888-315-6472
NEDIC 1-866-633-4220, Toronto 416-340-4156, nedic@uhn.ca; 211 Ontario (call or text 2-1-1); ConnexOntario 1-866-531-2600 or text CONNEX to 247247

ui:pages.mentalHealth.recovery.title: Alcohol, drugs and recovery
keyPoints: Cites CAMH: alcohol withdrawal can cause seizures and severe withdrawal can be fatal untreated, so ask a doctor before stopping daily heavy drinking
Quotes Sahih al-Bukhari 6780 ('Do not curse him... he loves Allah and His Messenger'); after a slip, 'repent and start again the same day'
Calls AA and NA 'not faith-based' (their 12 steps refer to God or a Higher Power); says Millati Islami lists no group in Canada
Cites Dr. Jibran Khokhar (Western) on relapse and stigma, and Dr. Zohair Abdul-Rahman (Yaqeen) on Ibn al-Qayyim's recovery programme

ui:pages.getHelp.crisis.title: Crisis line banner
keyPoints: 'If you are in danger, call 911. For a mental health crisis, call or text 9-8-8.' (911 first)
Frames 9-8-8 as the line for any mental health crisis; 988.ca presents it as the Suicide Crisis Helpline
Links to the mental health page for more support

ui:pages.getHelp.whatFor.title: What you can ask us for
keyPoints: Describes a mentor as 'a trained volunteer, usually of the same gender, who checks in with you'; confirm training and matching practice
Says 'If we are not the right people to answer, we will tell you who is'
Lists four request types: a question, a mentor, events and community, or a concern about a mentor, group or admin
ui:pages.getHelp.whatFor.label: Get help page > What you can ask us for

ui:pages.getHelp.form.title: Send a request (what the form asks)
keyPoints: Lists 8 things the form asks, incl. same-gender mentor preference, time zone and a consent line; the privacy policy lists only help type, language, contact and city
Says the form opens on Google Forms in a new tab
'We only ask what we need to reply and, if you want one, to find you a mentor'
ui:pages.getHelp.form.label: Get help page > Send a request (what the form asks)

ui:pages.getHelp.whoReads.title: Who reads it / When we reply
keyPoints: Says one or two volunteer coordinators read every request from one shared inbox and 'Nobody else sees it' (answers are also stored by Google)
Mentor match: the coordinator tells you first and passes on only what the mentor needs, once you agree
Reply target 48 to 72 hours, 'a target, not a promise', slower over holidays and in Ramadan
ui:pages.getHelp.whoReads.label: Get help page > Who reads it / When we reply

ui:pages.getHelp.privacy.title: Your privacy
keyPoints: Says a request reveals religion so it is treated as sensitive; only coordinators read it; not shared with family or a masjid without asking
Says Google may store answers outside Canada (Google Workspace offers only US or EU data regions)
Retention target: delete six months after closing (the privacy policy says the period is still to be confirmed)
Safety tip for private converts: use another device such as a library computer, and a contact method only you can see
ui:pages.getHelp.privacy.label: Get help page > Your privacy

ui:pages.getHelp.report.title: Report a mentor, group or admin
keyPoints: Asks users to report a mentor, member or admin who asks for money, proposes marriage, pushes them to join something or makes them feel unsafe
Says reports go to the coordinators, never to the person being reported
Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre 1-888-495-8501 for scams (the CAFC asks people to contact local police first)
ui:pages.getHelp.report.label: Get help page > Report a mentor, group or admin

ui:pages.communityGroups.reveals.title: What each option shows about you
keyPoints: Channel: number private; an admin sees it only if they already saved you as a contact; only you see which channels you follow
Group: admins see your number, other members may too, and anyone in the group can message you
Community: number visible to its admins and people who already have it, not to every member
Says WhatsApp is slowly rolling out usernames that hide your number; a dated claim to recheck
ui:pages.communityGroups.reveals.label: Community groups page > What each option shows about you

ui:pages.communityGroups.safety.title: If you are keeping your conversion private
keyPoints: Advises private converts to follow the channel rather than join a group, because the channel keeps the number hidden
Warns that group names and messages can appear in notifications, so think about who can see your phone
ui:pages.communityGroups.safety.label: Community groups page > If you are keeping your conversion private

ui:pages.communityGroups.rules.title: Group rules
keyPoints: Rules: no asking for money, selling or fundraising; no marriage proposals or matchmaking; no unsolicited private messages; no forwarding members' details
Admins are volunteers in a set role, not named individuals; they approve members, remove scam accounts and pass safety concerns to coordinators
ui:pages.communityGroups.rules.label: Community groups page > Group rules

ui:pages.communityGroups.report.title: Reporting a problem
keyPoints: Tells users to report anyone who asks for money, proposes marriage, messages privately without being asked or shares their details

ui:pages.communityGroups.report.label: Community groups page > Reporting a problem
